adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal, after a successful enable request (`if (response.status === 200) { setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes); return; }`), `onEnable()` is no longer called immediately. The only place `onEnable()` is invoked in the new flow is the explicit “close” button inside the `DisplayBackupCodes` step (`onClick -> resetState(); onEnable();`). There is no handler tied to `Dialog`/`onOpenChange` to call `resetState()` (or `onEnable()`) when the dialog is dismissed via ESC/X/overlay while on `DisplayBackupCodes`, so the component can remain in the `DisplayBackupCodes` step and the parent may not be notified of successful enable unless the user clicks that Close button.

adjudication.rationale: In `TwoFactor.tsx`, the six inputs are registered as separate RHF fields (`name={\`2fa${index + 1}\`}`), while the forms (login + disable modal) only clear `totpCode` when switching flows (`methods.setValue("totpCode", "")` in `login.tsx`, and `form.setValue("totpCode", "")` in `DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx`). This diff introduces UI toggles that unmount/remount `<TwoFactor />` (switching to `<BackupCode />` via `twoFactorLostAccess`), so the `2fa1`–`2fa6` fields can retain stale values in RHF and re-appear prefilled on remount even though `totpCode` was cleared. If `totpCode` is derived only via input change events (implied by the local `value` state in `TwoFactor.tsx`), remounting with prefilled digits can leave `totpCode` empty and cause submissions to behave as if no 2FA code was provided (e.g., server returns `SecondFactorRequired`).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds backup-code flows for login/disable and introduces the MissingBackupCodes error/message (login.tsx and DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx) when user.backupCodes is null (next-auth-options.ts and /api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts). Backup codes are only generated/stored during the 2FA setup endpoint (/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts) and then displayed once in EnableTwoFactorModal (SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes). The diff does not show any UI/endpoint to generate/regenerate backup codes for users who already had 2FA enabled before this change (and thus have backupCodes null after the migration), making the “generate them in your settings” guidance potentially unactionable for that cohort. This is an edge-case/product flow gap rather than a clear functional regression in the new code paths themselves.

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx`, the form uses `useForm<LoginValues>({ resolver: zodResolver(formSchema) })` and the PR adds a new `backupCode` field/flow (`LoginValues.backupCode`, `BackupCode` component registers `backupCode`, and next-auth `authorize` checks `credentials.backupCode`). However, this diff does not show any corresponding update to `formSchema` to include `backupCode`. With a Zod resolver, fields not in the schema are typically stripped from the submitted values, which would prevent `backupCode` from being passed to `authorize`, causing the backup-code path to never be taken and users to remain in the TOTP-required branch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup code single-use enforcement is racy (TOCTOU): consumption in `next-auth-options.ts` (~lines 131-155) is a non-atomic read-decrypt → indexOf → null-out → re-encrypt → `prisma.user.update` with no transaction or optimistic lock, so concurrent sign-ins can reuse the same code or resurrect a consumed code

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, backup-code login does a non-atomic sequence: decrypt `user.backupCodes` (from an earlier read), `indexOf` the submitted code, mutate the in-memory array (`backupCodes[index] = null`), then `prisma.user.update` with the re-encrypted whole array. There is no transaction, row lock, or conditional/optimistic check tying the update to the original value/version. Two concurrent sign-ins can both validate the same code before either update commits (allowing single-use bypass), and concurrent sign-ins with different codes can cause lost updates (last write wins), effectively “resurrecting” a code consumed by the other request.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unvalidated `backupCode` type crashes the disable endpoint: `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll(...)` in `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` (~line 57) is only truthiness-checked, so any truthy non-string from a JSON body throws an unhandled TypeError resulting in a 500 (same pattern in `next-auth-options.ts` ~line 141)

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, the backup-code branch is entered on a truthy check (`user.twoFactorEnabled && req.body.backupCode`), then immediately calls `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")`. If `backupCode` is any truthy non-string JSON value (e.g., `{}` or `[]`), `replaceAll` is not a function and will throw, resulting in an unhandled 500. The same pattern exists in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` where `credentials.backupCode.replaceAll(...)` is called after only checking `credentials.backupCode` truthiness, so malformed credential types can crash authorization.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup codes are compared in non-constant time: `Array.prototype.indexOf` in `disable.ts` and `next-auth-options.ts` short-circuits on the first differing character, creating a timing oracle on a secret comparison; should use constant-time comparison (e.g., compare SHA-256 digests via `crypto.timingSafeEqual`)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces backup-code verification by decrypting an array of codes and searching with `Array.prototype.indexOf` on a user-supplied string in both `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` (`const index = backupCodes.indexOf(req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""));`) and `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` (`const index = backupCodes.indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""));`). This performs normal string equality checks and stops on the first match, which is not constant-time and can create a timing side-channel for a secret comparison; constant-time comparison (e.g., `crypto.timingSafeEqual` over fixed-length buffers/digests) would avoid this.

In the auth flow, if a 2FA-enabled user supplies a backup code but `user.backupCodes` is null, `authorize()` throws `ErrorCode.MissingBackupCodes` (`next-auth-options.ts`), which `login.tsx` maps to the message "No backup codes found. adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-atomic backup-code consumption in next-auth-options.ts (~137-155): read-modify-write without a transaction or atomic update, so two concurrent logins with the same code can both succeed and two concurrent logins with different codes can silently resurrect a code (last-write-wins), breaking the documented 'exactly once' guarantee

adjudication_records.issue_text: disable.ts:~57 / next-auth-options.ts:~143 — backup-code input is neither normalized nor validated at the boundary: no toLowerCase() or trim() despite codes being stored as lowercase hex, so uppercase or whitespace-padded input fails during account recovery; additionally req.body.backupCode / credentials.backupCode are untyped any, so a non-string payload makes .replaceAll throw a TypeError → 500 instead of a 400

adjudication.rationale: The new backup-code paths assume a string and only do `.replaceAll("-", "")` without trimming/normalizing case. In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, `req.body.backupCode` is used directly and `.replaceAll` will throw if a non-string truthy value is sent (e.g. object/number), causing a 500 rather than a controlled 400. Similarly in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, `credentials.backupCode.replaceAll(...)` is called without a type guard. Also, backup codes are generated as lowercase hex (`crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")`), but input is not `trim()`’d or lowercased, so uppercase or whitespace-padded codes will not match and will incorrectly fail recovery.

adjudication_records.issue_text: next-auth-options.ts:~146-155 — backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write (decrypt → set null → re-encrypt → prisma.user.update); two concurrent sign-ins with the same code can both read the pre-write blob and both succeed, breaking the single-use invariant; needs a transaction or atomic conditional update

adjudication.rationale: In packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts, the new backup-code path for 2FA performs a non-atomic read/modify/write: it decrypts user.backupCodes, checks for credentials.backupCode, then sets backupCodes[index] = null and writes the whole encrypted blob back via prisma.user.update({ where: { id: user.id }, data: { backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(...) } }). Because there is no transaction or conditional/atomic update tied to the specific code value/version, two concurrent sign-ins using the same backup code could both read the same pre-update blob, both pass the index check, and both succeed, violating the intended single-use invariant.

This is a type/contract mismatch rather than a clear runtime break (JSON.stringify omits `undefined` properties), but it’s a real, diff-grounded review concern that should be documented/enforced or made optional in types.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write (decrypt → indexOf → mutate array → prisma.user.update) with no transaction or locking, so concurrent logins can both use the same code or a lost update can resurrect a spent code, breaking the single-use guarantee

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, backup code usage is implemented as a read-modify-write sequence: decrypt `user.backupCodes` → `indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))` → mutate `backupCodes[index] = null` → `prisma.user.update({ data: { backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(JSON.stringify(backupCodes), ...) }})`. There is no transaction, row-level lock, or optimistic concurrency check tying the update to the prior read, so concurrent login attempts can both validate the same backup code against the same decrypted array and both proceed, breaking the intended single-use guarantee / causing lost updates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: No backfill for existing 2FA users, who get backupCodes = NULL; the 'Lost access' recovery path shown to them always returns MissingBackupCodes with misleading guidance to generate codes in settings, which locked-out users cannot reach

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a nullable `backupCodes` column (migration + `schema.prisma`), but only populates it during `/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup` for newly setting up 2FA. Existing users with `twoFactorEnabled=true` will keep `backupCodes=null` (no backfill shown). The new “Lost access” paths (login: renders `<BackupCode />` when `twoFactorLostAccess` is toggled; server: `authorize` throws `MissingBackupCodes` when `!user.backupCodes`; disable endpoint returns `MissingBackupCodes`) will therefore deterministically fail for those existing 2FA users, and the UI string advises generating codes in settings (`missing_backup_codes`), which is not actionable for someone who is already blocked at the 2FA challenge. This is a real diff-grounded product/rollout gap (migration/backfill + UX), not a code correctness defect per se.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: onEnable() and resetState() are only called by the Close button in EnableTwoFactorModal, so dismissing the dialog via ESC or overlay click at the backup-codes step leaves parent settings state stale (2FA appears disabled) and re-exposes backup codes when the dialog is reopened

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal, successful enable no longer calls onEnable(); it only does `setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes)` (handleEnable, response.status===200). The only place that later calls `onEnable()` and `resetState()` is the “close” button inside the DisplayBackupCodes step. However, the Dialog is controlled by `open`/`onOpenChange`, and there is no handler to reset internal state or call onEnable when the dialog is dismissed via ESC/overlay click (i.e., onOpenChange to false). That would leave `step` as DisplayBackupCodes and `backupCodes` populated, so reopening can re-show codes, and the parent may remain stale (2FA enabled on server but parent not updated).

adjudication_records.issue_text: TOCTOU race on backup-code consumption in next-auth-options.ts:131-155: the read-decrypt-modify-write is non-atomic (no transaction, optimistic locking, or conditional write), so concurrent requests can both consume the same code and both log in successfully, or a lost update can resurrect a spent code, breaking the single-use guarantee

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, the backup-code path decrypts `user.backupCodes`, checks membership, then mutates the array and writes it back via `prisma.user.update` (read → verify → modify → write). This is not done in a transaction/conditional update, so concurrent authorize requests can both validate the same backup code before either update commits (allowing multiple logins with a “single-use” code). Additionally, concurrent consumption of different codes can lead to a lost update where the later write overwrites the earlier nulling, effectively resurrecting a spent code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup codes are permanently unrecoverable if the EnableTwoFactorModal dialog is dismissed via ESC or the X button: only the explicit Close button calls onEnable(), so dismissing otherwise closes the modal with no confirmation the codes were saved, no re-display mechanism exists, and the parent's 2FA state doesn't refresh

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal, after successful enable (handleEnable: response.status===200) it sets `step` to `SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes` instead of calling `onEnable()`. The only place that calls `onEnable()` in that step is the explicit “Close” button handler (`backup-codes-close`). The Dialog itself is controlled via `open`/`onOpenChange={onOpenChange}`, but this component does not wrap `onOpenChange` to (a) prevent closing during `DisplayBackupCodes`, (b) call `onEnable()`, or (c) reset state. So if the modal is dismissed via the Dialog’s standard close mechanisms (e.g., ESC / close button handled by `onOpenChange`), the parent won’t get `onEnable()` and the backup codes screen is lost; additionally, there’s no code in this diff that re-displays existing backup codes later (they’re only returned from `/totp/setup`).

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `ErrorCode.MissingBackupCodes` with the user-facing string: "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings." (en/common.json) and returns that error when `user.backupCodes` is null during backup-code disable/login (disable.ts and next-auth authorize). In the diff, the only place backup codes are generated is the TOTP setup endpoint (`/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts`), which also (re)sets `twoFactorSecret` and sets `twoFactorEnabled: false` as part of the setup flow. There is no separate "regenerate backup codes" path shown for an already-2FA-enabled account that simply lacks `backupCodes`, so the recovery advice can be misleading/unhelpful for existing 2FA users (especially if they’re trying the new “Lost access” path). This is a concrete product/edge-case gap grounded in the diff, but it’s not a strictly verifiable functional break without seeing the settings UX around re-running setup while 2FA is enabled.
